Hi Kimberly —

We're seeing a recurring set of discrepancies between the usage events Cumulus sent to AWS Marketplace and the fulfillment records that arrived in our billing system. The attached cumulus-metering-errors.log shows about 12% of events failing signature validation on your side (signature mismatch) and ~7% where the SKU in the webhook doesn't match the SKU that AWS reports back in the fulfillment call. That mismatch is triggering a manual reconciliation process on our end and delaying invoices.

Two asks: can you confirm the exact HMAC header and secret rotation window that Redwood expects for webhook verification? Also, we proposed a SKU mapping (attached proposed-sku-mapping.csv) because our internal product SKUs are nested (seat_count + premium-addon) — does Redwood support a proxy SKU translation before forwarding to AWS?

We want to avoid duplicate charge windows; our finance team prefers a deterministic reconciliation cutover (PRORATE window) to ensure partial-month seat changes are billed correctly.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

— Lauren

Hi Lauren — thanks for the samples and the mapping draft. Filing this with our marketplace ops and eng teams. Quick answers up-front:

- Signature: Redwood expects an X-Redwood-Signature header with HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body using the secret assigned to your seller account. We support a 48-hour overlap window for secret rotations by default (we can tighten to 24h if you need).
- SKU proxying: We do have a translation layer that can canonicalize nested SKUs into a single marketplace SKU at the gateway, but it requires a deterministic mapping table and an idempotent key to avoid duplicate fulfillment calls.
- Proration: Our default reconciliation uses AWS usage timestamps and a 1-hour aggregation window for seat changes; that can be expanded to a daily cutover if both sides prefer deterministic invoices.

Action items I'm proposing below — looping in Aditya and Monica to own technical and partner ops next steps.

Best,
Kimberly
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick tech notes after a brief dive into the logs:

1) Signature mismatches: the majority are due to minor canonicalization differences — Cumulus is applying JSON pretty-printing before HMAC, while our verifier computes the HMAC over the exact bytes we receive. We require the sender to compute HMAC over the UTF-8 bytes of the raw payload (no pretty-print). We also tolerate either X-Redwood-Signature or X-Amazon-Signature for a 48h overlap.

2) SKU mismatches: the proposed-sku-mapping.csv looks fine but two rows need canonicalization: your nested key for premium-addon uses ‘addon_v2’ while AWS expects ‘addon-v2’. Small normalization; we can add a normalization step at the gateway (lowercase, replace _ with -) but this adds a 2–5ms op and requires the mapping file to include both the canonical marketplace SKU and the seller SKU.

3) Idempotency: to prevent double fulfillment calls we need each webhook to provide a stable event_id (UUID) and a timestamp. If Cumulus can include event_id in the payload we will store a 7-day dedupe cache.

Proposed next steps (technical):
- Cumulus to update HMAC to compute over raw bytes (we can share a small Python snippet).
- Cumulus to normalize SKU rows and resend a CSV with marketplace_sku column.
- Redwood to enable SKU normalization at gateway for a rollout period of 3 days while monitoring error rate.

I'll drop sample code and the normalization test harness to the shared drive link. If those changes are quick we can test in the sandbox environment this week.

— Aditya
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Lauren — looping in AWS Marketplace Seller Support to confirm the expected marketplace-side SKU canonical forms and whether AWS will accept a proxy SKU mapping at the seller gateway (some partners have had success with a 1:1 mapping table).

Couple of operational clarifications from Redwood Ops:
- Proration window: Cumulus requested deterministic monthly proration at invoice cutover. We can support a daily cutover (00:00 UTC) for the first billing cycle to simplify reconciliation; after that we can switch to an hourly window if desired. Please confirm which you prefer.
- Secret rotation: we'll provide a short-lived onboarding secret and support a 48h overlap; for stricter security we can do 24h but it requires both sides to coordinate clock skew.
- Go-live plan: sandbox verification -> 3-day soft rollout (routing proxy active, dedupe on) -> go-live. During the soft rollout we'll keep detailed logs and a webhook replay tool available if issues arise.

Lauren, can you confirm the daily cutover for the first month? If yes, we'll schedule a sandbox test on Wed the 20th.

Thanks,
